name: VulnFanatic-NG
description: LLM-assisted vulnerability research over Binary Ninja decompiler output.
longdescription: VulnFanatic-NG adds a sidebar panel that scans the current binary in up to three phases. Phase 1 finds calls to dangerous functions (strcpy, memcpy, system, ...) and builds a decompiler-centric context (call path, path constraints, the calling function body, arguments, the called function's declared prototype, and tainted-source hints) for each call site. Phase 2 (when symbols/variable names are available) locates security-sensitive code (authentication, cryptography, signing, ...). Phase 3 (opt-in and online-only) audits firmware for missing or weak hardware-attack hardening controls (fault-injection / side-channel mitigations). Each context is sent to an LLM together with a tailored prompt; only confirmed issues are reported. Findings are listed with clickable references that navigate the view to the vulnerable code, and can be triaged (Real Issue / False Positive) and exported as fine-tuning data. The LLM backend is fully configurable in Settings (OpenAI-compatible by default, plus Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, and Azure OpenAI) and is typically a locally hosted model. An offline (no-LLM) programmatic Phase 1 mode is also available.
